title: Adversarial Robustness and Tropological Bias: Mapping AI Vulnerability onto Narrative Structure
text:
Adversarial testing in machine learning models, which involves intentionally introducing subtle perturbations to inputs to force prediction errors, mandates a re-evaluation of model stability. This technical necessity creates an unusual intersection with the study of rhetoric and literary theory.

By viewing an adversarial attack as an input perturbation—a meticulously designed flaw that exposes hidden fault lines in decision boundaries—it becomes comparable to tropological mapping in classical literature. A tropos, or figurative device, subtly shifts meaning by violating expected conventions; similarly, a successful adversarial sample exploits the inherent assumptions and feature weighting of the model, much like how subtle narrative deviations (e.g., unreliable narration) dismantle the reader's assumed understanding of truth.

The connection highlights that bias detection is not solely about correcting quantitative disparities in outcomes but rather about mapping epistemological vulnerabilities. Just as classical narratives teach readers to question obvious truths via literary tropes, algorithmic testing forces system builders and ethicists to acknowledge which deeply embedded, structural assumptions underpin the model's seemingly stable knowledge base.
